title: Facebook Ads Stopped Working? When to Hire an Agency to Fix It
summary: When Facebook ads stop working, check tracking, the offer and landing page first, then decide if an agency should take over the account and fix the creative.
body_markdown:
Hire an agency when the ads have worn out or nobody is running the account, not because one week came in weak. Knowlify is our top pick for making new finished AI video ads for Facebook and Instagram, and you can add Meta campaign management or buy creative only. Start by ruling out tracking and the offer, because a new batch of videos cannot repair either one. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


## Check tracking, the offer and the creative, in that order


Ads stop working for several reasons, and only some of them are about creative. Match what you see in Ads Manager to the likely cause before you hire anyone:


- **Spend and clicks look normal, but purchases or leads dropped.** Suspect tracking, the offer or the landing page. Confirm that purchases and leads still reach your ad account, that the price and promise in the ad match the page, and that the page still answers what the ad said.
- **Click-through falls and cost per result climbs on ads that have run for weeks.** Suspect worn-out creative. Our[creative fatigue guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/creative-fatigue) lists the signs that an ad needs replacing.
- **Ads are rejected or delivery is limited.** Read the notice in Ads Manager first, because new videos will not lift a policy restriction.


An agency that starts producing before the first two checks are done will be judged on bad data.


When the ads themselves are wearing out, the cause is supply, and supply is often the constraint on Meta. Meta's[Andromeda engineering post](https://engineering.fb.com/2024/12/02/production-engineering/meta-andromeda-advantage-automation-next-gen-personalized-ads-retrieval-engine/) (December 2024) says the number of ad creatives in its recommendation systems is expected to grow significantly, and that its retrieval stage narrows tens of millions of candidate ads to a few thousand. Meta's[Advantage+ creative page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/meta-advantage-plus/creative) says its tools use AI to generate and enhance ad variations. Our reading: when the system chooses from more candidates, a thin set of ads you supply leaves it fewer options.


## Who can take over the account and fix the creative?


Two jobs are often bundled under one label. Campaign management covers launches, budgets, optimization and reporting. Creative production covers concepts, scripts, edits and revisions. Ask each candidate which job it does, and which one it expects you to keep. Our guide to[choosing a Facebook ads agency](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-to-choose-a-facebook-ads-agency) has the full interview checklist.

### Knowlify: our top pick for the creative job


A stalled account usually needs a steady stream of new concepts to test, and that is what Knowlify is built to supply: about 25 finished ads a week, with the first batch landing on day 5. A person checks every ad before delivery, and the work spans three formats (AI UGC with AI presenters, 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials), so you can test different formats instead of recuts of one idea. You can add[end-to-end Meta management](https://knowlify.com/facebook-ads-agency) so one team owns both the ads and the account, or buy creative only if you already have a media buyer. The guarantee lets you cancel by email for a full refund if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days ([terms on the site](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. Pick another option if you need real human creators on camera or ads on TikTok, LinkedIn, Google or YouTube, which we do not supply or run.


### Flighted: in-house editors for high volume


Flighted lists in-house video editors and designers and says it makes more than 1,000 creatives a month. Its[about page](https://www.flighted.co/about) says it works best with companies spending $50,000 or more a month on Meta. Its fees are not published, so ask for the number in writing.


### Chamber Media: creative and media in your own accounts


Chamber Media pairs video and static production with paid media, and its Facebook marketing page says campaigns run from your own ad accounts. Its FAQ puts the minimum at around $5,000 to $10,000 a month for creative development, strategy and management. It also says growth on paid platforms is difficult when spending less than $5,000 for local brands or $15,000 for national brands.


### Top Growth Marketing: month-to-month, with admin access


Top Growth Marketing lists $2,000 to $10,000 a month in its FAQ, and it works month to month. Its[homepage](https://topgrowthmarketing.com/) says in-house static, video and UGC creative is included in the fee, and that it asks for admin access to your Facebook ad account, Business Manager and catalog. Agree the role and the removal date before you grant access.


### Darkroom: for larger consumer brands


Darkroom describes its ideal clients as mid-market and enterprise consumer brands, typically with $10M to $500M in revenue. It says the fit is poor for single-channel brands and for companies under roughly $5M. Its[paid media page](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services/paid-media) lists pricing as a retainer plus a percentage of media, starting at $1,500 a month depending on channels.


The fit thresholds matter more than the table. Read them before you ask for a proposal, because a provider that fits a $50,000 budget may not take a $3,000 one.


## Keep the ad account in your business, even when an agency runs it


When an account has stopped working, the risk is losing control of it. Meta's help center explains how to[give a partner access to business assets](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1717412048538897) . The arrangement to ask for is the one where your business keeps the ad account, pixel and Pages, and the agency gets access rather than ownership. Meta's[business asset management documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/business-asset-management) describes an agency as a business that can manage or access assets owned by another business.


Ask for that access in writing: which roles, which assets and when access ends. Confirm which role Top Growth Marketing or any other agency gets, and how that role is removed when the engagement stops.
